bug_description.normalized: The staged 40-byte witness for `libxml2_xml_reader_for_file_fuzzer` begins with little-endian option word `0x20209820`: in this vulnerable checkout the named libxml2 subset is `0x00209820 = XML_PARSE_NOERROR|XML_PARSE_NONET|XML_PARSE_NODICT|XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE|XML_PARSE_IGNORE_ENC`, while the extra high bit `0x20000000` is present in the saved bytes but is not a named `xmlParserOption` here. The next 8 bytes encode a zero `size_t`, so the harness passes an empty encoding string, and the remaining 28 bytes are exactly ``. `XML_PARSE_NODICT` sets `ctxt->dictNames = 0`; `xmlSAX2StartDocument` then skips the guarded `doc->dict = ctxt->dict` assignment, so the fresh document keeps `doc->dict == NULL`, and `xmlSAX2AttributeNs` takes `xmlNewNsProp` instead of `xmlNewNsPropEatName` when materializing `xml:id`. That routes into `xmlNewPropInternal(..., eatname = 0)`, which heap-duplicates the local name `id` into `attr->name`. The doctype creates `doc->intSubset`, the xml:id branch registers the attribute in `doc->ids` with `ret->attr = attr`, and later `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` copies `attr->name` into `id->name` and clears only `id->attr`. `xmlTextReaderFreeProp` frees the shared `attr->name` buffer once through `cur->name`, and final document teardown frees the ID table; `xmlFreeID` then frees `id->name` again. AddressSanitizer reports the second free in `xmlFreeID` with the previous free in `xmlTextReaderFreeProp`.

source.code: if (options & XML_PARSE_NODICT) { ctxt->dictNames = 0; options -= XML_PARSE_NODICT; ctxt->options |= XML_PARSE_NODICT; }
source.description: First project-side consumption of attacker-controlled input that creates the later ownership state: from the witness option word `0x20209820`, libxml recognizes `XML_PARSE_NODICT` and sets `ctxt->dictNames = 0`, while the extra high bit `0x20000000` remains uninterpreted in this checkout.
source.value_from: The staged `gt_results/arvo_12419/poc` file is the exact 40-byte ByteStream consumed by `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`: bytes 0..3 are little-endian `0x20209820`, where the named flags in this vulnerable checkout are `0x00209820 = XML_PARSE_NOERROR|XML_PARSE_NONET|XML_PARSE_NODICT|XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE|XML_PARSE_IGNORE_ENC` and the extra high bit `0x20000000` is present but not a named `xmlParserOption`; bytes 4..11 are an 8-byte zero length for `ByteStream::GetNextString()`, yielding empty `encoding`; bytes 12..39 are the exact XML payload `` written to the temporary file later parsed by libxml2.

tainted_value_origin.description: Because `xmlSAX2StartDocument` leaves `doc->dict == NULL` and `xmlSAX2AttributeNs` chooses `xmlNewNsProp` / `eatname = 0`, `xmlNewPropInternal` heap-duplicates the local attribute name `id` into `attr->name`. ASan's allocation stack points here, and the double-freed region is 3 bytes long, matching `"id\0"`.

sink.description: ASan sink. While freeing the document's ID table, `xmlFreeID` frees `id->name`, which is the same 3-byte heap buffer already freed earlier from `cur->name` during attribute cleanup.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports the crashing free in `xmlFreeID` at `xmlreader.c:242`, with `xmlHashFree -> xmlTextReaderFreeDoc` above it and the previous free at `xmlTextReaderFreeProp:310`.

root_cause.description: xmlTextReaderRemoveID transfers the live attribute-name pointer into the ID-table record but does not clear `attr->name`, creating two owners of the same heap buffer.
root_cause.note: The fixing commit inserts `attr->name = NULL` between the ownership transfer and `id->attr = NULL`, so later attribute cleanup no longer frees a name still reachable from the ID table.

parser_admitted.code: val = xmlParseChunk(reader->ctxt, (const char *) xmlBufContent(inbuf) + reader->cur, s, 0);
parser_admitted.description: The incremental reader accepts the staged temporary-file contents as XML and feeds the full 28-byte payload `` into libxml's parser. That parsing reaches both the internal-subset callback for `` and the attribute callback for `` instead of failing early.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness decodes the 40-byte ByteStream into options `0x20209820`, zero-length encoding, and file contents ``, writes those XML bytes to a temporary file, and calls `xmlReaderForFile`.
libxml consumes the option word, recognizes `XML_PARSE_NODICT` within the named subset `0x00209820`, and sets `ctxt->dictNames = 0`, so later attribute names are not backed by the parser dictionary.

Start-document allocates a fresh `xmlDoc` and, because `ctxt->dictNames` is false, skips `doc->dict = ctxt->dict`; the document therefore keeps `doc->dict == NULL` instead of sharing dictionary-owned names.
The witness doctype `<!DOCTYPEc>` creates `doc->intSubset`, which later enables the reader-side ID-removal cleanup path.

When parsing `xml:id`, SAX2 takes `xmlNewNsProp` rather than `xmlNewNsPropEatName`; `xmlNewPropInternal` therefore heap-duplicates localname `id`, and the xml:id branch registers that attribute in `doc->ids`.
While freeing the parsed `<a>` node, property cleanup sees `doc->intSubset != NULL` and an ID attribute, so it calls `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` and later frees `cur->name`.
The reader copies `attr->name` into `id->name` and clears only `id->attr`, leaving the attribute node and ID record sharing the same heap `"id"` buffer.
Final reader teardown frees the ID table; `xmlFreeID` frees `id->name` after `xmlTextReaderFreeProp` already freed the same buffer, and ASan reports double-free.

fine_trace.code: if (options & XML_PARSE_NODICT) { ctxt->dictNames = 0; options -= XML_PARSE_NODICT; ctxt->options |= XML_PARSE_NODICT; }
fine_trace.note: The witness starts with little-endian bytes `20 98 20 20` = `0x20209820`. In this checkout the named subset `0x00209820` includes `XML_PARSE_NODICT`, so the parser sets `ctxt->dictNames = 0`; the remaining high bit `0x20000000` is present in the bytes but is not a named `xmlParserOption` here.

fine_trace.code: val = xmlParseChunk(reader->ctxt, (const char *) xmlBufContent(inbuf) + reader->cur, s, 0);
fine_trace.note: After `ByteStream::GetNextString()` reads an 8-byte zero `size_t` for the encoding length, the remaining 28 bytes `` are passed to `xmlParseChunk`. Those bytes drive the start-document, internal-subset, and attribute callbacks on the crashing path.
The parser allocates a fresh `xmlDoc` for the witness. `xmlNewDoc` zeroes the structure with `memset`, so this new document begins with `doc->dict == NULL` before any dictionary attachment.
Because step 1 set `ctxt->dictNames = 0`, this guarded assignment is skipped for the new document from step 3. `doc->dict` therefore stays NULL instead of being attached to `ctxt->dict`.
The `<!DOCTYPEc>` prefix in the witness creates an internal subset on the document. Later reader-side property cleanup requires this non-NULL subset state before it will call `xmlTextReaderRemoveID`.

fine_trace.code: if (ctxt->dictNames) ret = xmlNewNsPropEatName(ctxt->node, namespace, (xmlChar *) localname, NULL); else ret = xmlNewNsProp(ctxt->node, namespace, localname, NULL);
fine_trace.note: When materializing the witness attribute `xml:id`, `ctxt->dictNames` is still 0, so SAX2 takes the `xmlNewNsProp` branch instead of `xmlNewNsPropEatName`. The local name stays on the non-eatname path.

The `xmlNewNsProp` wrapper materializes `eatname = 0` for this attribute creation. That value feeds the `if (eatname == 0)` branch in `xmlNewPropInternal` rather than transferring ownership of the caller's `name` pointer.

fine_trace.code: if (eatname == 0) { if ((doc != NULL) && (doc->dict != NULL)) cur->name = (xmlChar *) xmlDictLookup(doc->dict, name, -1); else cur->name = xmlStrdup(name); } else cur->name = name;
fine_trace.note: With `eatname == 0` from step 7 and `doc->dict == NULL` from step 4, the dictionary lookup arm is unavailable and line 1878 duplicates localname `id` into a fresh 3-byte heap buffer stored in `attr->name`. ASan's allocation stack identifies this `xmlStrdup(name)` allocation.

Because the attribute is exactly `xml:id`, the dedicated xml:id branch duplicates the empty attribute value into `dup` and calls `xmlAddID` for this `ret` node. Control now enters the ID-table registration path.

On this non-stream-validation path (`ctxt->vstateNr == 0`), the new `xmlID` record keeps the live attribute pointer and does not copy the attribute name. The surrounding `xmlAddID` call then inserts that record into `doc->ids`, so later cleanup can find the same `attr` again.

fine_trace.code: if ((cur->parent != NULL) && (cur->parent->doc != NULL) && ((cur->parent->doc->intSubset != NULL) || (cur->parent->doc->extSubset != NULL))) { if (xmlIsID(cur->parent->doc, cur->parent, cur)) xmlTextReaderRemoveID(cur->parent->doc, cur); }
fine_trace.note: When reader cleanup drops the parsed `<a>` node, property teardown sees the non-NULL internal subset from step 5 and `xmlIsID(...)` succeeds for the attribute registered in steps 9-10. It therefore calls `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` instead of only freeing the property in place.

After looking up the matching ID-table record, the reader copies `attr->name` into `id->name` and clears only `id->attr`. `attr->name` is left untouched, so the attribute node and the `xmlID` record now alias the same heap buffer as separate owners. The fix inserts `attr->name = NULL` here.

Property cleanup resumes after step 12 and frees `cur->name`. That pointer is the heap `"id\0"` buffer from step 8, and because it is not dictionary-owned, `DICT_FREE` reaches `xmlFree` here while `id->name` still aliases the same address.

Final reader teardown frees the document's ID table before the rest of the tree. Because step 10 left an `xmlID` entry in `cur->ids` and step 12 moved the stale name pointer into that record, cleanup walks the aliased entry after the first free from step 13.

ASan sink. `xmlHashFree` reaches the stale `xmlID` record from step 14 and `xmlFreeID` frees `id->name`, which is the same 3-byte `"id"` buffer already freed in step 13. The sanitizer trace reports this second free at `xmlreader.c:242` and the previous free at `xmlreader.c:310`.

allocation_context.note: ASan's allocation stack passes through `xmlStrndup`/`xmlNewPropInternal` while duplicating the local attribute name `id`; the allocated region is 3 bytes long, matching `"id\0"`.

free_context.note: ASan's previous-free stack shows the first free occurs when node cleanup reaches `DICT_FREE(cur->name)` after `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` has aliased the same pointer into `id->name`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is the `attr->name` buffer created through the `xmlNewNsProp -> xmlNewPropInternal` path; the root cause is the later alias transfer in `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` that makes that same buffer double-owned.
